Anatoly 0.4.0 adds explainable version hypotheses and broader technology inventory while preserving the boundary between remote observations, exact version declarations and PHP2Shell assessment.

- Produce bounded `version_hypotheses` when complete versions are unavailable, with qualitative confidence, reasons, observed sources, references and limitations. Repeated responses do not increase confidence, and alternative ranges remain alternatives.
- Distinguish Laravel welcome-template generations and native exception-renderer families with conjunctive DOM patterns. Customized, retained or backported views can differ from the installed framework; version ranges remain hypotheses, and conflicting explicit declarations remain visible.
- Retain visible Laravel/PHP version declarations from contextual native welcome footers as well as exception panels. Masked welcome pages do not supply exact version evidence.
- Extend custom header, cookie, asset and HTML fingerprints with validated conditional range metadata. Use `--no-hypotheses` to disable these proposals without removing exact evidence or technology recognition.
- Inventory valid production Composer/npm packages beyond the built-in product mappings, including legacy npm lockfiles, while keeping requirements, resolved tags and runtime versions distinct.
- Observe WordPress plugin/theme identities and numeric asset cache hints without assigning those values as installed component versions.
- Retain allowlisted diagnostic component versions and guard phpinfo/error-footer recognition against hidden, inert and documentary examples.
- Promote disclosed diagnostics ahead of pending guesses, avoid redundant redirect-driven diagnostic requests, respect HTML base URLs and preserve received header evidence when a body is incomplete.
- Keep provenance visible in JSON, terminal, HTML, explanation, comparison and watch output, with bounded retention and explicit coverage gaps.

Framework compatibility requirements, cookies and asset patterns cannot establish a running PHP patch level. No hypothesis establishes a CVE verdict or security certification. Anatoly does not send exploit, memory-exhaustion or command-execution payloads.

## Laravel validation

32 real HTTP checks passed across independently attested Laravel 8.83.29, 9.52.21, 10.48.29, 11.8.0, 11.9.0, 12.28.0, 12.70.2 and 13.0.0 installations. Each installation supplied native welcome and error pages with visible and redacted version numbers.

Masked welcome pages distinguished the shared 8/9 family, 10.x, 11.x, the shared modern 12/13 family and the 13.x template when its specific changelog link was present. Native welcome footers and supported exception renderers retained exact declarations when visible. Masked exception renderers yielded family ranges; legacy error pages without Ignition remained unknown. Template families cannot identify arbitrary patch releases. Large error pages explicitly reported bounded HTML coverage.

## Downloads

- Linux x86_64 and ARM64: glibc >= 2.35, OpenSSL 3 and CA certificates.
- Windows x86_64: native Windows TLS trust store.
- `SHA256SUMS` covers all platform archives and `install.sh`.
- Archives include the fingerprint catalog, its authoring guide and reconnaissance documentation.

Download the archive for your platform and verify its SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS`. Checksums verify download integrity; they are not independent publisher signatures.

For Linux or an existing Exegol installation, download and inspect the release installer:

```sh
curl -fL https://github.com/lucasschimmel/anatoly/releases/download/v0.4.0/install.sh -o /tmp/anatoly-install.sh
less /tmp/anatoly-install.sh
sh /tmp/anatoly-install.sh --version v0.4.0 --bin-dir "$HOME/.local/bin" --force
"$HOME/.local/bin/anatoly" --version
```

Keep the same `--bin-dir` as your existing installation. Omit `--force` for a new installation. The installer verifies the archive checksum, preserves existing binaries without `--force`, and does not change shell configuration or scan targets.

See [docs/detection-and-fingerprints.md](https://github.com/lucasschimmel/anatoly/blob/v0.4.0/docs/detection-and-fingerprints.md) for custom catalogs and recognition limits. [docs/exegol.md](https://github.com/lucasschimmel/anatoly/blob/v0.4.0/docs/exegol.md) describes persistent container installation; this independent release does not add Anatoly to Exegol's official images.

The PHP advisory policy remains dated 2026-10-31. Native CI and release jobs run formatting, Clippy and platform tests; Linux jobs also validate real loopback HTTPS and installer behavior.
